questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question: A rigid body is in complete mechanical equilibrium when:
options: Only the net force on it is zero
Both the net force and the net torque on it are zero
Only the net torque on it is zero
questions.explanation: Zero net force prevents translation and zero net torque prevents rotation. A couple is the case where the net force is zero but the torque is not, so the body still spins.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 6: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The speed of sound in air increases with a rise in temperature because the speed is proportional to:
options: The square root of the absolute temperature
questions.explanation: v ∝ √T, so the speed rises by about 0.61 m/s for each degree rise in temperature. It is independent of pressure, because density changes in step with pressure.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The torque acting on a rectangular current loop of N turns, area A, carrying current I, placed with its plane parallel to a uniform magnetic field B, is:
questions.explanation: τ = NIAB sin θ, where θ is the angle between the magnetic moment and the field. With the plane parallel to B, the moment is perpendicular to B, so sin θ = 1 and the torque is maximum.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 4: Moving Charges and Magnetism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Atoms of different elements having the same mass number but different atomic numbers are called:
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers, isobars the reverse, and isotones have the same number of neutrons.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 2: Structure of Atom

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The work done by a gas during free expansion into a vacuum is:
options: Zero, because the external pressure is zero
questions.explanation: W = -P(ext)ΔV, and with P(ext) = 0 there is nothing to push against. If the expansion is also adiabatic, then Q = 0 as well, so ΔU = 0 and the temperature does not change.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The integrated rate equation for a first order reaction is k = (2.303/t) log([A]₀/[A]). A plot of log[A] against time therefore gives a straight line whose slope is:
questions.explanation: Rearranging gives log[A] = log[A]₀ - (k/2.303)t, so the line falls with slope -k/2.303 and the rate constant can be read straight off the graph.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The membrane that bounds the large central vacuole of a mature plant cell is called the:
questions.explanation: The vacuole can occupy up to 90 percent of the cell's volume, and the tonoplast actively pumps ions into it, so the vacuole holds a far higher concentration than the cytoplasm.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Cyclosporin A, used as an immunosuppressive drug in organ transplant patients, is obtained from:
questions.explanation: Monascus purpureus yields statins, which lower blood cholesterol by competitively inhibiting the enzyme that makes it.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 8: Microbes in Human Welfare

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: A deficiency of antidiuretic hormone in humans leads to a condition called:
options: Diabetes insipidus, with the passing of large volumes of dilute urine
questions.explanation: Without ADH the kidney cannot reabsorb enough water, so the patient passes litres of dilute urine and is constantly thirsty. Diabetes mellitus is instead a failure of insulin.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 19: Chemical Coordination and Integration

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The acrosome of a human sperm is important at fertilisation because it:
options: Provides energy for the sperm's movement
Contains enzymes that help the sperm penetrate the layers around the ovum
Forms the tail of the sperm
questions.explanation: The acrosome is a cap derived from the Golgi apparatus. Energy comes from the mitochondria of the middle piece, and the genetic material lies in the head's nucleus.
